notes.Howard the Duck: The first film based on a Marvel comic book to reach cinemas. An alien duck is torn from his planet and ends up in Cleveland. A legendary flop at the time, a cult object now.
notes.The Punisher (1989): Dolph Lundgren as Frank Castle, a policeman who becomes a vigilante after the mob kills his family. A hard, direct version, with no connection to the rest of Marvel.
notes.Captain America (1990): A low-budget adaptation of Captain America, frozen in the '40s and thawed out in the present. A historical curiosity more than anything else.
notes.Blade: Wesley Snipes as the half-vampire vampire hunter. Many consider this the film that proved Marvel could work at the cinema, opening the way for X-Men and Spider-Man.
notes.Blade II: Directed by Guillermo del Toro. Blade has to ally himself with the vampires themselves to stop the Reapers, a mutant strain that threatens both species.
notes.Hulk (Ang Lee): Ang Lee's version, more psychological and formally daring, with editing in comic-book panels. Not part of the MCU.
notes.Daredevil: Ben Affleck as the blind lawyer Matt Murdock. Established Kingpin and Elektra in cinema, with a noir Hell's Kitchen tone.
notes.Blade: Trinity: Blade joins the Nightstalkers to face Dracula. Closes out the trilogy and features Ryan Reynolds in one of his first approaches to the Deadpool style.
notes.The Punisher (2004): Thomas Jane as Frank Castle, in a reboot set in Florida. Closer to the tone of methodical revenge from the comics.
notes.Elektra: A Daredevil spin-off with Jennifer Garner. Elektra, resurrected, becomes an assassin and ends up protecting those she was supposed to kill.
notes.Man-Thing: A low-budget horror film about Marvel's swamp creature. Released direct to television in the US.
notes.Ghost Rider: Nicolas Cage as Johnny Blaze, the biker who sold his soul to the devil and turns into Ghost Rider.
notes.Punisher: War Zone: An even more violent reboot, with Ray Stevenson. Frank Castle against Jigsaw, in a register that is almost ultraviolent comic book.
notes.Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance: A sequel directed by the Crank duo. Johnny Blaze hides out in Eastern Europe and has to protect a boy from the devil himself.
notes.X-Men: First Class: The origin: Charles Xavier and Erik Lehnsherr meet and form the first team of mutants during the Cuban Missile Crisis. This is where the friendship that defines the whole saga begins — and breaks.
notes.X-Men: Days of Future Past: Wolverine is sent from an apocalyptic future to 1973 to prevent the assassination that gives rise to the Sentinels. This film rewrites the timeline and erases several events from the earlier films.
notes.X-Men Origins: Wolverine: Logan's story from the 19th century to the Weapon X programme. Sits in a grey area of the timeline after Days of Future Past rewrote everything.
notes.X-Men: Apocalypse: The first mutant, En Sabah Nur, awakens and gathers his Four Horsemen. Jean Grey, Cyclops and Nightcrawler join the X-Men as youngsters.
notes.Dark Phoenix: Jean Grey is taken over by a cosmic force during a space mission. The last film of the Fox era of X-Men before the Disney acquisition.
notes.X-Men: The film that kicked off the modern era of superheroes. Rogue and Wolverine are taken in by Xavier's school while Magneto builds a machine to turn world leaders into mutants.
notes.X2: X-Men United: Colonel Stryker attacks the school and the X-Men are forced to ally with Magneto. Ends with Jean Grey's sacrifice and the foreshadowing of the Phoenix.
notes.X-Men: The Last Stand: A cure for the mutant gene divides the world, and Jean returns as Dark Phoenix. Several main characters die — events later undone by Days of Future Past.
notes.The Wolverine: Logan travels to Japan to say goodbye to a man he saved in Nagasaki. A more intimate film, about grief and immortality.
notes.The New Mutants: Five young mutants are confined in an isolated facility and realise they're trapped. Gothic horror within the X-Men universe.
notes.Deadpool: Wade Wilson, a mercenary with terminal cancer, is subjected to an experiment that cures him and disfigures him. Breaks the fourth wall constantly and is the first big Marvel hit for adults.
notes.Deadpool 2: Deadpool forms X-Force to protect a young mutant from Cable, a soldier from the future. Ends up using the time device to fix his own history.
notes.Logan: The end of the line. In a future where almost no mutants remain, an aged Logan and an ailing Xavier protect a girl with his powers. The definitive farewell to the Fox era.
notes.Fantastic Four (2005): A cosmic storm gives powers to four astronauts — and to Victor Von Doom. Light, family-friendly tone, with Chris Evans as the Human Torch before he was Captain America.
notes.Rise of the Silver Surfer: The Silver Surfer arrives on Earth as Galactus's herald. Reed and Sue's wedding is constantly interrupted by the end of the world.
notes.Fant4stic (2015): A dark reboot in which the foursome gain their powers in an alternate dimension. A troubled production that resulted in one of the worst-received Marvel films ever.
notes.Madame Web: Cassandra Webb, a New York paramedic, discovers she can see the future and tries to protect three young women destined to become heroes.
notes.Spider-Man (2002): Sam Raimi and Tobey Maguire define the template for the modern superhero film. Peter Parker is bitten by a spider and learns that great power brings great responsibility.
notes.Spider-Man 2: Peter loses his powers from emotional exhaustion while facing Doctor Octopus. Often cited as one of the best superhero films ever made.
notes.Spider-Man 3: The black symbiote corrupts Peter, and Venom and Sandman enter the picture. Overloaded, but a central piece of the nostalgia for the Raimi trilogy.
notes.The Amazing Spider-Man: A reboot with Andrew Garfield, centred on the relationship with Gwen Stacy and the mystery of Peter's parents. The villain is the Lizard.
notes.The Amazing Spider-Man 2: Electro and the Green Goblin attack New York, and the film culminates in Gwen Stacy's death — the moment Garfield would go on to revisit in No Way Home.
notes.Venom: Journalist Eddie Brock fuses with an alien symbiote. The relationship between the two is treated almost like a dysfunctional romantic comedy.
notes.Venom: Let There Be Carnage: Serial killer Cletus Kasady gets his own symbiote, Carnage. The post-credits scene throws Eddie into the MCU, tying in with No Way Home.
notes.Morbius: A biochemist with a rare blood disease cures himself with bat DNA and becomes a living vampire.
notes.Kraven the Hunter: Sergei Kravinoff becomes the world's greatest hunter after a near-fatal encounter with a lion, and turns against his own criminal father.
notes.Venom: The Last Dance: Eddie and Venom flee both the authorities and creatures sent by Knull. The end of the trilogy.
notes.Into the Spider-Verse: Miles Morales is bitten by a spider and discovers there are Spider-Men from various dimensions. Revolutionised animation and won the Oscar.
notes.Across the Spider-Verse: Miles crosses the multiverse and confronts the Spider Society and the idea that certain tragic events are mandatory in a Spider-Man's life.
notes.Captain America: The First Avenger: Steve Rogers, rejected by the army, becomes the first super-soldier and takes on the Red Skull and HYDRA. Ends with him frozen in Arctic ice.
notes.Captain Marvel: Carol Danvers discovers her memory has been manipulated by the Kree. Features a younger Nick Fury and the Tesseract, and explains the origin of the name 'Avengers'.
notes.Iron Man: The film that started it all. Tony Stark is kidnapped in Afghanistan, builds a suit of armour to escape, and decides to publicly claim the Iron Man identity.
notes.Iron Man 2: Tony is being poisoned by his own reactor and takes on Ivan Vanko. S.H.I.E.L.D. begins assembling the Avengers Initiative in the background.
notes.The Incredible Hulk: Bruce Banner is on the run through Brazil while searching for a cure and is pursued by General Ross. Ends with the confrontation against the Abomination in Harlem.
notes.Thor: Thor is banished from Asgard to Earth without his powers and has to learn humility while Loki takes the throne.
notes.The Avengers: Loki opens a portal above New York and Nick Fury brings the team together for the first time. The Battle of New York becomes the reference event for the whole MCU.
notes.Thor: The Dark World: Jane Foster is infected by the Aether and the Dark Elves return. Formally introduces the second Infinity Stone.
notes.Iron Man 3: Tony suffers panic attacks after New York and loses everything. The Mandarin turns out to be a hoax.
notes.Captain America: The Winter Soldier: S.H.I.E.L.D. has been infiltrated by HYDRA from within. Steve discovers that the Winter Soldier is Bucky. A political thriller that changed the tone of the MCU.
notes.Guardians of the Galaxy: A group of space outlaws teams up to stop Ronan from using an Infinity Stone. Opened up the cosmic and comic side of the MCU.
notes.Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: Peter Quill meets his father, Ego, and realises his true father was always Yondu. Set just a few months after the first film.
notes.Avengers: Age of Ultron: Tony creates an artificial intelligence that decides humanity is the problem. Vision, Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver are born.
notes.Ant-Man: Thief Scott Lang inherits Hank Pym's Ant-Man suit. A small-scale heist in the middle of an ever-bigger universe.
notes.Captain America: Civil War: The Sokovia Accords split the Avengers down the middle. Introduces the MCU's Black Panther and Spider-Man, and breaks up the team before Thanos arrives.
notes.Black Widow: Natasha, on the run, confronts her past in the Red Room and reunites with her fake family from childhood.
notes.Spider-Man: Homecoming: Peter Parker tries to prove himself worthy of the Avengers while facing the Vulture, a contractor ruined by the post-New York clean-up.
notes.Black Panther: T'Challa takes the throne of Wakanda and is challenged by Killmonger, whose fury is born from his own country's isolationism.
notes.Doctor Strange: An arrogant neurosurgeon loses the use of his hands and discovers the mystic arts at Kamar-Taj. Introduces the Time Stone.
notes.Thor: Ragnarok: Hela destroys Thor's hammer and Asgard falls. Taika Waititi reinvents the saga's tone as colourful comedy — and reunites Thor with the Hulk on Sakaar.
notes.Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos gathers the six Infinity Stones and wipes out half of all life in the universe with a snap of his fingers. The heroes lose.
notes.Ant-Man and the Wasp: Scott and Hope search for Janet van Dyne in the Quantum Realm. The post-credits scene leaves Scott trapped there during the Blip.
notes.Avengers: Endgame: Five years later, the survivors use the Quantum Realm to travel through time and retrieve the Stones. Culminates in Tony Stark's sacrifice and Steve Rogers's farewell.
notes.Spider-Man: Far From Home: Peter, on holiday in Europe and dealing with grief over Tony, is manipulated by Mysterio — who reveals his identity to the world.
notes.Shang-Chi: Shang-Chi confronts his father, the real Mandarin, and the legacy of the Ten Rings. Set after the return of the people who had vanished.
notes.Eternals: A group of immortal beings lived hidden on Earth for millennia without interfering in human history. Explains why they never showed up during Thanos's snap.
notes.Spider-Man: No Way Home: A badly cast spell opens up the multiverse and brings villains — and Spider-Men — from other realities. The whole world forgets who Peter Parker is.
notes.Multiverse of Madness: Strange protects America Chavez while Wanda, corrupted by the Darkhold, crosses realities to find her children again.
notes.Thor: Love and Thunder: Jane Foster becomes the Mighty Thor while Gorr the God Butcher wipes out deities across the universe.
notes.Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: After T'Challa's death, Wakanda faces Namor and the underwater kingdom of Talokan. Shuri takes up the mantle.
notes.Quantumania: The Lang family is sucked into the Quantum Realm and encounters Kang the Conqueror — the first major introduction of the multiversal threat.
notes.Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: Rocket's tragic origin is finally revealed, and the team faces the High Evolutionary. The end of this line-up of the Guardians.
notes.The Marvels: Carol Danvers, Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan swap places whenever they use their powers and have to learn to work together.
notes.Deadpool & Wolverine: Wade Wilson is recruited by the TVA and drags a Wolverine from another reality on a trip through the Void. Officially brings the Fox era into the MCU.
notes.Captain America: Brave New World: Sam Wilson, now Captain America, finds himself at the centre of an international incident with President Thaddeus Ross.
notes.Thunderbolts*: A group of anti-heroes and former villains is forced to work together on a mission booby-trapped by Valentina Allegra de Fontaine.
notes.The Fantastic Four: First Steps: The Fantastic Four on an alternate Earth with a 1960s aesthetic, facing Galactus and the Silver Surfer.
notes.Spider-Man: Brand New Day: Peter Parker starts over from scratch in a world where nobody remembers him, rebuilding his life and identity.
notes.Avengers: Doomsday: The convergence of the multiverse's timelines, with Doctor Doom as the central threat. The endpoint of the whole Multiverse Saga.
notes.The Amazing Spider-Man (1977): The first live-action Spider-Man series, with Nicholas Hammond. Modest in its effects and with almost none of the comic-book villains, but the first time Peter Parker existed in live action.
notes.The Incredible Hulk (1978): Bill Bixby as David Banner and Lou Ferrigno as the Hulk. A weekly fugitive series, more melancholy than heroic, and for decades the most popular Marvel adaptation ever.
notes.X-Men: The Animated Series: The cartoon that shaped an entire generation. Adapted dense comic-book arcs like The Dark Phoenix Saga and Days of Future Past, without simplifying them.
notes.Spider-Man: The Animated Series: The animated Spider-Man of the '90s, with a long continuity and a final saga that was already playing with the multiverse.
notes.Blade: The Series: A television continuation of the Blade films, with Kirk 'Sticky Fingaz' Jones in the role. Lasted a single season.
notes.The Gifted S1: A family discovers their children are mutants and joins an underground network. Set in a world where the X-Men have disappeared.
notes.The Gifted S2: The Inner Circle becomes radicalised and the conflict between mutants and humans escalates. The series ended here.
notes.Legion S1: David Haller, institutionalised since he was young, discovers that the voices he hears aren't schizophrenia. Visually the boldest Marvel series ever made.
notes.Legion S2: David confronts the Shadow King while the series itself questions whether he's hero or villain.
notes.Legion S3: Time travel, a new character capable of it, and an ending that rewrites David's life from birth.
notes.Daredevil S1: Matt Murdock, blind lawyer by day and vigilante by night, takes on Wilson Fisk. Changed the tone of what a Marvel series could be: violent, Catholic and centred on guilt.
notes.Jessica Jones S1: A private detective with super-strength and post-traumatic stress is hunted by the man who mind-controlled her. Kilgrave is one of the best Marvel villains in any format.
notes.Daredevil S2: The Punisher and Elektra both arrive in Hell's Kitchen at the same time, forcing Matt to define his limits.
notes.Luke Cage S1: A bulletproof man in Harlem becomes the symbol of a neighbourhood. Strongly anchored in New York's Black culture and music.
notes.Iron Fist S1: Danny Rand returns to New York fifteen years after being presumed dead, with the iron fist and a company to reclaim.
notes.The Defenders: The four heroes team up against the Hand. The mini-series that was the goal of the whole Netflix phase.
notes.The Punisher S1: Frank Castle dismantles the military conspiracy behind his family's death. More a war thriller than a superhero series.
notes.Jessica Jones S2: Jessica investigates the origin of her own powers and finds her mother, alive and even more violent than she is.
notes.Luke Cage S2: Bushmaster challenges Luke for control of Harlem, and Luke himself starts becoming the thing he used to fight.
notes.Iron Fist S2: Davos takes the iron fist and Colleen Wing takes centre stage. Considerably better received than the first.
notes.Daredevil S3: A Born Again adaptation: Fisk methodically destroys Matt's life from prison, and Bullseye enters the picture. The high point of the whole Netflix phase.
notes.The Punisher S2: Frank protects a teenage girl while Billy Russo returns as Jigsaw.
notes.Jessica Jones S3: A meticulous killer forces Jessica and Trish to choose between justice and revenge. Closed out the Netflix era.
notes.Agent Carter S1: Peggy Carter, underused at the post-war SSR, investigates alone while everyone treats her like a secretary. Elegant and furious.
notes.Agent Carter S2: Peggy moves to Los Angeles and takes on Zero Matter. Ends with her laying the groundwork for the founding of S.H.I.E.L.D.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S1: Coulson puts together a small team — and halfway through the season HYDRA reveals itself, in sync with the Winter Soldier. The turn that saved the series.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S2: S.H.I.E.L.D. rebuilds itself in secret and the Inhumans enter the story with Skye's transformation.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S3: Hive, an ancient Inhuman, returns from another planet in Grant Ward's body.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4: Divided into three blocks: Robbie Reyes's Ghost Rider, the LMD artificial intelligence, and the virtual world Framework.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5: The team is thrown into a future where Earth has been destroyed and has to figure out how to prevent it.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S6: Without Coulson, the team deals with a lookalike of him and a threat from another planet.
notes.Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7: The final season crosses decades of alternate history, from the '30s to the '80s. A generous send-off for seven years.
notes.Inhumans: Attilan's royal family, exiled in Hawaii after a coup by Maximus. A single season, poorly received.
notes.Runaways S1: Six teenagers discover their parents are part of a murderous cult and run away from home. One of the best Marvel adaptations for a young audience.
notes.Cloak & Dagger S1: Tyrone and Tandy, linked since childhood by an accident, gain complementary powers in New Orleans.
notes.Runaways S2: The kids live in an abandoned mansion while trying to expose the Pride.
notes.Cloak & Dagger S2: The duo investigates a human trafficking ring. Crosses over with Tandy and Tyrone in a more adult register.
notes.Runaways S3: The final season brings a crossover with Cloak & Dagger and resolves the Pride arc.
notes.Helstrom: Two siblings, children of a demonic serial killer, hunt down the worst of humanity. Lasted one season.
Stop-motion animation about the villain with the giant head dealing with divorce and the bankruptcy of his own evil organisation.
notes.Hit-Monkey S1: A Japanese macaque trained by the ghost of a professional assassin avenges his troop in Tokyo.
notes.Hit-Monkey S2: The monkey moves to New York and keeps killing, now with a new ghost as his advisor.
notes.Loki S1: The variant of Loki who escaped with the Tesseract in 2012 is captured by the TVA. The series that formally opened up the MCU multiverse and introduced He Who Remains.
notes.WandaVision: Wanda, grieving, traps an entire town inside sitcoms from several decades. Marvel Studios' first series, and still one of the best.
notes.The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: Sam and Bucky deal with the post-Blip world and a new government-appointed Captain America. Ends with Sam accepting the shield.
notes.Hawkeye: Clint Barton just wants to get home in time for Christmas, but Kate Bishop and his past as Ronin won't let him. Brings Kingpin into the MCU.
notes.Moon Knight: A museum employee with a dissociative disorder shares his body with a mercenary and serves an Egyptian god. The series most isolated from the rest of the MCU.
notes.Echo: Maya Lopez returns to the Choctaw community and confronts Kingpin. The first series under the Marvel Spotlight label, closer to the Netflix tone.
notes.She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: Jennifer Walters gains her cousin's powers and works in superhuman law. A legal comedy that breaks the fourth wall.
notes.Ms. Marvel: Kamala Khan, a Jersey City teenager and Avengers fan, discovers powers linked to the history of the Partition of India.
notes.Ironheart: Riri Williams returns to Chicago and finds herself caught between the technology she builds and the Hood's magic.
notes.Werewolf by Night: A black-and-white Halloween special, shot like a '40s Universal horror film.
notes.The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Spec: Drax and Mantis kidnap Kevin Bacon as a Christmas present for Quill. Short, absurd and genuinely touching.
notes.Secret Invasion: Nick Fury returns to Earth to stop a faction of Skrulls infiltrated within world governments.
notes.Loki S2: The TVA falls apart as the temporal loom collapses. Loki ends up single-handedly holding together every timeline.
notes.Agatha All Along: Agatha Harkness gathers a coven of witches to walk the Witches' Road. A direct sequel to WandaVision.
notes.Daredevil: Born Again S1: Matt Murdock tries to live only as a lawyer while Wilson Fisk runs for Mayor of New York. Picks up directly from the Netflix series.
notes.Wonder Man: Simon Williams, a Hollywood actor, goes for the lead role in a superhero film. Industry satire, with Trevor Slattery back.
notes.Daredevil: Born Again S2: The show's second season, with the city under Fisk's control and the Punisher back in the field.
notes.The Punisher: One Last Kill: A special centred on Frank Castle, following the events of Born Again.
notes.Eyes of Wakanda: An anthology about Wakandan warriors sent through history to recover stolen vibranium artefacts. The earliest point in the whole MCU timeline.
notes.I Am Groot S1: Shorts about baby Groot getting into trouble aboard the Guardians' ship.
notes.I Am Groot S2: Five more shorts, in the same vein and equally dialogue-free.
notes.What If...? S1: The Watcher observes alternate realities: Peggy as a super-soldier, T'Challa as Star-Lord, a zombie MCU. Ends with the Guardians of the Multiverse.
notes.Marvel Zombies: An expansion of the zombie episode of What If...?, now as its own series and considerably more violent.
notes.What If...? S2: A new round of alternate realities, including a Happy Hogan Christmas and a version of New York in 1602.
notes.What If...? S3: The final season, which closes out the arc of the Watcher and the animated multiverse.
notes.X-Men '97 S1: A direct continuation of the '90s animated series, picking back up the original style and voices. Responded to the grief over Xavier and was acclaimed.
notes.X-Men '97 S2: The second season, following on from the first's devastating finale.
notes.Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man S1: An alternative origin for Peter Parker, mentored by Norman Osborn instead of Tony Stark, with an aesthetic inspired by 1960s comic books.
